notes: US state law follows the IIHS table, with service status from robotaxi trackers. Most non-US records rest on secondary trackers, law-firm notes and press, not regulators. Tesla "unsupervised" means the Tesla Robotaxi fleet in Texas and Florida only. No customer-owned car runs unsupervised. Robotaxi markers show one record per city with the most advanced operator status, and cities with testing but no riders are marked announced. Chinese cities beyond the big four and several factory locations rest on older or secondary sources.

ARE.summary: WeRide and Uber run fully driverless paid rides in Abu Dhabi and Dubai; a federal self-driving law was approved in 2026.

AUS.summary: The national Automated Vehicle Safety Law is not yet in force and is targeted for 2027; Tesla FSD Supervised is on sale.

AUT.summary: Austria has made no national decision on Tesla FSD and is waiting for an EU-wide vote.

BEL.summary: Tesla FSD Supervised was approved in June 2026; the Leuven autonomous shuttle still carries a safety officer.

BRA.summary: Brazil has no autonomous vehicle law; Bill 1317/2023 is still pending in Congress.

CAN.summary: Rules are provincial: Ontario runs a testing pilot to 2027 and British Columbia bans Level 3 and above; Waymo plans Toronto for 2028.

CHE.summary: A March 2025 ordinance allows driverless vehicles on approved routes under remote supervision; services are still in testing.

CHN.summary: Driverless robotaxis from Baidu, Pony.ai and WeRide carry the public in Wuhan, Beijing, Guangzhou and Shenzhen under city permits.

CZE.summary: Czechia recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in September 2026 for driver-supervised use.

DEU.summary: A 2021 law allows Level 4 driverless operation in approved areas with a permit, but no regular service runs yet; FSD awaits an EU decision.

DNK.summary: Denmark recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in June 2026 and it is rolling out to customers.

ESP.summary: A national road-testing framework has applied since 2025; WeRide runs in Madrid with operators on board and Waymo plans riders in 2027.

EST.summary: A fixed-route shuttle at Tallinn airport runs with no operator on board; Estonia recognised Tesla FSD Supervised in May 2026.

FIN.summary: Finland recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised on 10 November 2026; rollout to customers was about to begin.

FRA.summary: Driverless vehicles may run only as automated road transport systems on set routes under a 2021 decree; Level 3 is allowed.

GBR.summary: Driverless passenger service permits opened in May 2026 under the Automated Vehicles Act 2024, but none is in use; Wayve rides in London have a safety driver.

HKG.summary: Pilot licences only, with a trained backup operator required; Baidu Apollo Go is testing with no public riders.

HRV.summary: Verne runs paid robotaxi rides in Zagreb with an operator on board, and driverless rides for invited passengers began in September 2026.

HUN.summary: Hungary has made no national decision on Tesla FSD and is following EU developments.

IDN.summary: Indonesia has no autonomous vehicle legislation and relies on existing traffic law.

IND.summary: India has no autonomous vehicle law and its transport minister has said driverless cars will not be allowed.

IRL.summary: No approval for Tesla FSD Supervised yet; Tesla is in talks with Irish regulators.

ISR.summary: Supervised trials only; the transport ministry expects rules for Level 4 robotaxis to take effect in the second half of 2027.

ITA.summary: Rules cover supervised road testing only; Italy has not recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD and backs an EU-wide decision.

JPN.summary: Level 4 driverless operation has been legal by prefectural permit since April 2023; Waymo plans public rides in Tokyo in 2027.

KAZ.summary: Rules issued in mid-2026 set a three-year pilot that allows driverless taxis in Astana, Almaty and Kosshy; service is planned for 2027.

KOR.summary: Paid autonomous rides are allowed only in designated pilot zones, and Seoul robotaxis still carry a safety supervisor.

LTU.summary: Lithuania recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in May 2026 and it is rolling out to customers.

LUX.summary: Luxembourg has authorised supervised testing only, including a 12-month Level 4 pilot with Pony.ai.

LVA.summary: Latvia recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in October 2026; rollout to customers was still pending.

MEX.summary: Mexico has no legal framework for autonomous driving and no federal bill; Tesla sells FSD Supervised there.

MYS.summary: Malaysia allows testing under transport ministry guidelines, with a public test route in Cyberjaya; its roadmap targets Level 3 by 2030.

NLD.summary: Driverless road experiments are allowed by permit, and the RDW approved Tesla FSD Supervised in April 2026, a first in Europe.

NOR.summary: A 2017 testing law governs trials; the Oslo pilot carries an operator on board, and Norway will follow the EU decision on Tesla FSD.

NZL.summary: There is no dedicated autonomous vehicle law, though existing law does not require a driver to be present; Tesla FSD Supervised is on sale.

POL.summary: Poland requires local testing before any approval of Tesla FSD Supervised.

PRT.summary: Portugal has not recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised.

QAT.summary: Pony.ai and Mowasalat run a public robotaxi service in Doha with a safety operator on board; driverless rides are invitation-only tests.

ROU.summary: Romania has not recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD; its road code bars drivers from releasing the steering wheel.

RUS.summary: Robotaxis run under experimental regimes with a safety driver; a draft law to remove the driver would take effect in September 2027.

SAU.summary: WeRide robotaxis run on Uber in Riyadh with operators on board under a transport authority trial.

SGP.summary: Grab and WeRide carry the public on approved routes in Punggol with a safety operator on board; Waymo plans driverless service in 2028.

SVK.summary: Slovakia recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in October 2026 for driver-supervised use.

SVN.summary: Slovenia approved Tesla FSD Supervised in September 2026 for driver-supervised use.

SWE.summary: Only limited tests with trained drivers are permitted; Tesla FSD has public road testing approval but customers cannot use it.

THA.summary: Thailand has no autonomous vehicle law; general traffic and vehicle law applies.

TUR.summary: A December 2024 regulation sets EU-style type approval for automated driving systems; no driverless service operates.

TWN.summary: Autonomous vehicles run only as time-limited sandbox trials under the 2019 unmanned vehicles experimentation act.

US-AK.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-AL.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver on board; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-AR.summary: Driverless operation is allowed under a state-approved program, with a licensed driver on board for the first six months.

US-AZ.summary: Waymo runs public driverless rides across metro Phoenix; state law lets Level 4 and 5 vehicles operate with no licensed driver.

US-CA.summary: Waymo carries the public driverless in the Bay Area, Los Angeles and San Diego under DMV and CPUC permits; Tesla still uses safety drivers.

US-CO.summary: Waymo driverless rides began in Denver in September 2026, by invitation at first; state law allows Level 4 and 5 deployment.

US-CT.summary: Testing pilot only under state statute, with a human operator required.

US-DC.summary: Testing only: a test operator must be in the vehicle at first, and paid service is not authorized; a robotaxi bill is before the Council.

US-DE.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-FL.summary: Waymo and Tesla Robotaxi both run driverless public rides in Miami, Orlando and Tampa; state law needs no permit or human driver.

US-GA.summary: Waymo driverless rides run in Atlanta through the Uber app; state law lets Level 4 and 5 vehicles operate with no licensed driver.

US-HI.summary: Testing only under a 2020 pilot law; Level 4 and 5 vehicles need a licensed driver on board.

US-IA.summary: State law allows deployment of automated driving system vehicles with no licensed driver on board; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-ID.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-IL.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; Waymo has named Chicago as a future city but nothing operates yet.

US-IN.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-KS.summary: State law allows driverless deployment, with a licensed driver on board for the first 12 months in most passenger vehicles.

US-KY.summary: State law allows Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver on board once a law enforcement plan is filed; no public service yet.

US-LA.summary: State law allows driverless commercial trucks only; other vehicles are not addressed. Waymo lists New Orleans as a future city.

US-MA.summary: Testing only under MassDOT agreements, with a licensed test driver in the vehicle; no AV statute.

US-MD.summary: Testing is allowed with a licensed driver in the vehicle; there is no deployment law. Waymo lists Baltimore as a future city.

US-ME.summary: State pilot rules cover testing only and do not require a licensed driver in the vehicle; no deployment law.

US-MI.summary: State law allows driverless testing and manufacturer-run on-demand networks; Waymo plans Detroit but no public service runs yet.

US-MN.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; May Mobility shuttles run with an operator on board and Waymo has announced Minneapolis.

US-MO.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-MS.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-MT.summary: A 2025 law allows Level 4 and 5 deployment subject to state rulemaking; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-NC.summary: State law allows Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; Waymo has named Charlotte as a future city but no service runs yet.

US-ND.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-NE.summary: State law allows Level 4 and 5 vehicles to operate with no operator present in the vehicle; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-NH.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver on board, subject to conditions; no public service yet.

US-NJ.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-NM.summary: Fully autonomous vehicles may run with nobody on board after a filing with the state transport department; no public service yet.

US-NV.summary: Zoox carries the public driverless on the Las Vegas Strip and Waymo rides are by invitation; paid service needs a state permit.

US-NY.summary: Testing pilot only, extended to April 2028; a licensed driver must be in the vehicle and there is no path to driverless service.

US-OH.summary: State rules cover testing only but allow it with no licensed driver in the vehicle; no deployment law or public service.

US-OK.summary: State law allows Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver given a law enforcement plan and $1 million cover; no service yet.

US-OR.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law beyond naming ODOT as lead agency; Waymo has named Portland as a future city.

US-PA.summary: Highly automated vehicles may run with no driver under a PennDOT certificate; Waymo has announced Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

US-RI.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-SC.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-SD.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-TN.summary: Waymo opened driverless rides to everyone in Nashville in June 2026; state law lets Level 4 and 5 vehicles run with no licensed driver.

US-TX.summary: Waymo and Tesla run driverless rides in Austin, Dallas, Houston and San Antonio; commercial driverless service needs TxDMV authorization.

US-UT.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-VA.summary: No general AV statute: the only law covers driverless work-zone crash trucks. A licensing bill was carried over to 2027.

US-VT.summary: Testing only; vehicles need a licensed driver on board and deployment is not addressed.

US-WA.summary: State law covers testing only and allows it with no human operator on board; commercial driverless service is not addressed.

US-WI.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-WV.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-WY.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

USA.summary: Law is set state by state: driverless robotaxis carry the public in eight states, while others allow testing only or have no AV law.

ZAF.summary: South Africa has no legislation for autonomous vehicles, which cannot use public roads until rules exist.

points.name: Dongfeng Nissan Huadu plant

points.name: GAC Toyota plant

points.name: Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Center Singapore
points.detail: Hyundai and Motional said in Nov 2023 the Ioniq 5 robotaxi is manufactured at HMGICS; current output not confirmed.

points.name: Holon Jacksonville plant
points.detail: 580,000 sq ft plant at Eastport Industrial Park; groundbreaking was set for Apr 2026, commissioning in late 2027.

points.name: Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America
points.detail: Builds autonomous-ready Ioniq 5 for Waymo; Hyundai said deliveries to Waymo begin in Q4 2026.

points.name: Jiangling Motors (JMC)
points.detail: JMC produces the Apollo RT6 for Baidu; the exact JMC plant is not named, so the point is the company home city.

points.name: Lucid AMP-1
points.vehicle: Lucid Gravity robotaxi for Uber and Nuro
points.detail: Gravity robotaxi with Nuro Driver for Uber; pre-production builds reported from Oct 2026, launch fleet to follow.

points.name: Roush autonomous truck upfit lines
points.vehicle: Aurora Driver International LT trucks; Kodiak Driver trucks
points.detail: Roush upfits driverless trucks for Aurora (target 20 a week by Dec 2026) and for Kodiak in Livonia.

points.name: Tesla Gigafactory Texas
points.detail: Cybercab pilot production from Feb 2026 and series production from Apr 2026, with no steering wheel or pedals.

points.name: Tesla Semi factory
points.detail: High-volume Semi line beside Gigafactory Nevada started in Apr 2026; Tesla targets an autonomous Semi in 2027.

points.name: Toyota Takaoka plant
points.detail: Toyota will build an autonomous bZ4X and fit the Waymo Driver on site, for Japan tests from 2027.

points.name: Verne factory
points.detail: 28,500 m2 plant in VGP Park Zagreb started in 2025 and was due to operate in 2026; start of production not confirmed.

points.name: VinFast Hai Phong plant
points.detail: Tensor says its Level 4 Robocar is built with VinFast; start of series production has not been confirmed.

points.name: Volvo New River Valley plant
points.detail: Volvo assembles the VNL Autonomous with redundant systems for the Aurora Driver at its NRV plant.

points.name: Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles Hanover plant
points.detail: Pre-series production of the autonomous ID. Buzz AD is under way; series production is due to start in 2027.

points.name: Waymo Driver Integration Plant
points.vehicle: Waymo Ojai, Hyundai Ioniq 5 and Jaguar I-PACE robotaxi integration
points.detail: Magna-run plant fitting the Waymo Driver; an Aug 2026 aerial count found 953 Ojai on the lot, 684 finished.

points.name: XPeng Guangzhou plant
points.detail: First series-production XPeng robotaxi rolled off the Guangzhou line in May 2026; pilot operations planned.

points.name: Yutong
points.detail: Yutong partnered with WeRide in 2020 to mass-produce autonomous minibuses; plant placed at Yutong home city.

points.name: Zeekr plant
points.detail: Zeekr builds the Ojai in Ningbo; customs data showed over 3,200 shipped to the US for Waymo fit-out in Mesa.

points.name: Zoox robotaxi plant
points.detail: Zoox builds its bidirectional robotaxi here; capacity reported at roughly 10,000 vehicles a year.

points.name: Abu Dhabi
points.detail: WeRide fully driverless on Uber since Nov 2025; Apollo Go driverless on Yas Island via AutoGo since Jan 2026.

points.name: Arlington
points.detail: May Mobility targets a commercial launch on Uber in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027; no launch confirmed.

points.name: Atlanta
points.detail: Waymo driverless on Uber since Jun 2025; May Mobility runs a Lyft pilot with standby operators; Zoox is testing.

points.name: Austin
points.detail: Waymo on Uber since Mar 2025; Tesla Robotaxi since Jun 2025 incl. Cybercab rides; Zoox rides for staff and friends only.

points.name: Baltimore
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Dec 2025 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Beijing
points.detail: Fully driverless fare-charging rides in Yizhuang from Pony.ai and WeRide; Apollo Go also operates driverless.

points.name: Berlin
points.detail: Five ID. Buzz AD vehicles on the road without passengers; rides for selected applicants not yet confirmed.

points.name: Boston
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Feb 2026 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Bratislava
points.detail: Robotaxis among vehicles announced in Mar 2026, with tests to start in Bratislava; no start confirmed.

points.name: Changsha
points.detail: Apollo Go open to the public since 2020; current share of rides without a safety operator is not confirmed.

points.name: Charlotte
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Feb 2026 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Chicago
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Feb 2026 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Chongqing
points.detail: Apollo Go commercial driverless service, first permitted in Yongchuan in Aug 2022; 2026 scope not confirmed.

points.name: Copenhagen
points.detail: Level 4 robotaxis for the public planned for the first half of 2027, pending Danish approvals.

points.name: Dallas
points.detail: Waymo open to all since Aug 2026; Tesla since Apr 2026; Avride on Uber with a safety driver; Zoox is testing.

points.name: Darmstadt
points.detail: Free on-demand KIRA rides for registered users since May 2025 in Darmstadt, Langen and Egelsbach, safety driver aboard.

points.name: Denver
points.detail: Waymo driverless rides since Sep 2026, with riders admitted from a waitlist.

points.name: Detroit
points.detail: Waymo began fully autonomous driving in Oct 2026 with rides limited to its own employees.

points.name: Doha
points.detail: Fare-charging Karwa service since Dec 2025; Pony.ai reported fully driverless rides in Sep 2026, scope not confirmed.

points.name: Dongguan
points.detail: Apollo Go filed a test and demonstration project planning to deploy 1,000 autonomous vehicles and a regional base.

points.name: Dubai
points.detail: WeRide and Apollo Go run fare-charging driverless rides in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim; Pony.ai is in driverless trials.

points.name: Eden Prairie
points.detail: May Mobility autonomous microtransit with SouthWest Transit; Minnesota law requires a licensed driver on board.

points.name: Fort Worth
points.detail: Tesla Robotaxi rides began 2 Nov 2026 in a zone of about 145 sq mi, reported as running without a safety monitor.

points.name: Foshan
points.detail: Apollo Go filed its South China operations headquarters and robotaxi demonstration project in Shunde.

points.name: Grand Rapids (Minnesota)
points.detail: Free on-demand goMARTI service run by May Mobility with an operator on board.

points.name: Guangzhou
points.operator: Pony.ai, WeRide, Didi, Apollo Go, Ruqi
points.detail: Pony.ai and WeRide run 24/7 driverless service across Huangpu, Tianhe and Haizhu; Didi runs a driverless trial.

points.name: Hamburg
points.detail: Free MOIA pilot since 15 Jul 2026 for registered residents, up to ten ID. Buzz AD with a safety operator.

points.name: Hangzhou
points.detail: Cao Cao runs robotaxis here and won approval in Apr 2026 as the first firm allowed driverless road tests in the city.

points.name: Hefei
points.detail: Apollo Go paid commercial pilot since Aug 2022; driverless status in 2026 is not confirmed.

points.name: Hong Kong
points.detail: Resident-only Tung Chung trial with a backup operator ran 21 Oct to 3 Nov 2026; driverless testing on Airport Island.

points.name: Houston
points.detail: Waymo open to all since Aug 2026; Tesla since Apr 2026; Zoox testing; Nuro/Lucid/Uber plan a mid-2027 launch.

points.name: Jacksonville
points.detail: Tesla lists Jacksonville as a coming-soon Robotaxi city with no launch date.

points.name: Jiangmen
points.detail: Apollo Go filed a test and demonstration project planning at least 90 intelligent connected vehicles.

points.name: Las Vegas
points.detail: Zoox paid driverless rides since Aug 2026; Waymo by waitlist; Motional on Uber with an operator; Tesla announced.

points.name: London
points.detail: Wayve cars on Uber since 3 Sep 2026 with a licensed driver; Waymo and Apollo Go testing; Pony.ai tests announced.

points.name: Los Angeles
points.detail: Waymo open to all since Nov 2024; Zoox and MOIA (ID. Buzz AD with Uber) are testing without public riders.

points.name: Luxembourg
points.detail: Twelve-month pilot from June 2026 aiming to be ready for driverless operation by its end; no public riders reported.

points.name: Madrid
points.detail: WeRide holds Spain's first national Level 4 permit (Sep 2026) for 20 supervised test cars; Waymo aims for 2027.

points.name: Manchester
points.detail: Announced as the Verne, Pony.ai and Uber partnership's next city after Zagreb, with tests under way.

points.name: Miami
points.detail: Waymo open to all since Apr 2026; Tesla Robotaxi since Jul 2026; Zoox rides for staff and friends only.

points.name: Minneapolis
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Nov 2025 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Munich
points.detail: Waymo announced Munich in Aug 2026 with public rides aimed for end of 2027; Uber plans with Momenta and Autobrains.

points.name: Nashville
points.detail: Waymo driverless rides open to the public in the Waymo app, and on Lyft since Sep 2026.

points.name: New Orleans
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Nov 2025 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: New York City
points.detail: Waymo has announced plans, but its testing permit expired on 31 Mar 2026 and no rides run.

points.name: Ordos
points.detail: Listed as a WeRide commercial robotaxi service since Nov 2023; whether cars run driverless is not confirmed.

points.name: Orlando
points.detail: Waymo open to all since Apr 2026; Tesla Robotaxi since Jul 2026.

points.name: Osaka
points.detail: Osaka and newmo signed an agreement in Apr 2026 to develop and deploy autonomous taxi services; no public rides yet.

points.name: Oslo
points.detail: Groruddalen pilot paused since Feb 2026 while ID. Buzz AD vehicles replace the first cars; riders to be re-invited.

points.name: Paris
points.detail: Pilot planned from 2028 in municipalities north-west of Paris, aiming for Greater Paris service by 2030.

points.name: Philadelphia
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Dec 2025 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Phoenix
points.detail: Waymo public driverless rides since 2020 across about 350 sq mi; Zoox is testing and Tesla has announced plans.

points.name: Pittsburgh
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Dec 2025 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Portland
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Apr 2026 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Ras Al Khaimah
points.detail: WeRide service announced; the company reported robotaxi and robobus pilot operations from late 2025.

points.name: Riyadh
points.detail: WeRide rides on Uber since Oct 2025 between Roshn Front and Princess Noura University, with a safety operator.

points.name: Sacramento
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Feb 2026 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: San Antonio
points.detail: Waymo open to all since 14 Oct 2026; Tesla Robotaxi started 9 Nov 2026 in a zone of about 274 sq mi.

points.name: San Diego
points.detail: Waymo open to all riders since 14 Oct 2026; Zoox began testing in Sep 2026.

points.name: San Francisco Bay Area
points.detail: Waymo open to all; Zoox driverless by waitlist; Tesla runs with a human driver; Nuro/Lucid/Uber employee rides only.

points.name: Seattle
points.detail: Waymo and Zoox are testing; Washington State has no framework for paid driverless rides.

points.name: Seoul
points.detail: Late-night autonomous taxis in Gangnam, paid since Apr 2026 and growing to 19 cars; Pony.ai plans service by 2028.

points.name: Shanghai
points.detail: Pony.ai fully driverless commercial service in Pudong (Jinqiao, Huamu) since Aug 2025; others also operate.

points.name: Shenzhen
points.detail: Pony.ai holds a citywide driverless commercial permit; Apollo Go driverless in Nanshan, Bao'an and Pingshan.

points.name: Singapore
points.detail: Free supervised rides in Punggol: WeRide/Grab Ai.R since Apr 2026, Pony.ai on Zig since Jun 2026. Waymo plans 2028.

points.name: St. Gallen
points.detail: Level 4 test permit for 80 km2; hands-free runs with safety drivers since 1 Jun 2026; regular service aimed for 2027.

points.name: St. Louis
points.detail: Waymo has been testing here since Dec 2025 with no public riders and no launch date.

points.name: Suzhou
points.detail: Listed as an announced WeRide robotaxi service area with no launch date.

points.name: Tampa
points.detail: Waymo open to all riders since 14 Oct 2026; Tesla Robotaxi since Jul 2026.

points.name: Tokyo
points.detail: Waymo is testing and targets driverless public rides in 2027; Wayve, Nissan and Uber plan a supervised pilot.

points.name: Toronto
points.detail: Waymo announced Toronto in Oct 2026, with mapping and supervised testing under way and first riders targeted for 2028.

points.name: Washington, DC
points.detail: Waymo (since Mar 2025) and Zoox are testing with no public riders.

points.name: Wuhan
points.detail: Largest Apollo Go fleet; free trial rides resumed Aug 2026 after a four-month suspension following an April outage.

points.name: Yangquan
points.detail: Apollo Go paid demonstration service since Feb 2022 in Chengqu and the High-tech Zone; 2026 status not confirmed.

points.name: Yokohama
points.detail: Nissan service in Minato Mirai from Oct 2026 with 10 cars and about 500 registered residents, safety driver on board.

points.name: Zagreb
points.detail: Paid rides since Apr 2026 with a safety operator; driverless rides for invited users on one 22 km route since 10 Sep.

points.name: Zhuhai (Hengqin)
points.detail: Ruqi said its robotaxi service covered the Hengqin cooperation zone as of Dec 2025; driver status not stated.

points.name: Zurich
